purpose: Deterministic candidate-development contracts for orthogonal public-information mechanisms. Design only; no performance, ranking, tuning, selection, promotion or live execution.

shared_contract.label: next_regular_session_5_trading_day_excess_return_vs_frozen_benchmark
shared_contract.decision_boundary: event_public_observation_boundary; if only a date is available, use next regular trading-session boundary and do not infer an intraday clock
shared_contract.exposure_mapping: frozen before outcome observation; issuer/entity mapping is immutable for the trial
shared_contract.universe: fresh symbol-disjoint research universe defined by the relevant trial contract

candidates.name: Therapeutic-substitution pressure
candidates.mechanism: A newly public shortage state creates operational substitution pressure across products sharing an ingredient/application or therapeutic-equivalence relationship; affected manufacturer exposure is the fixed economic transmission channel.
candidates.event_clock: earliest defensible public observation timestamp for the shortage record or explicitly documented next-publication boundary; occurrence time alone is not admissible.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: shift event availability forward by 1-5 sessions while holding the calendar fixed
shuffle issuer-exposure assignments within the frozen universe
replace public-observation time with occurrence time and require the candidate to show that the inference changes; otherwise reject clock discipline
future-mutation test on a historical shortage record

candidates.name: Inspection-to-enforcement escalation
candidates.mechanism: A transition from public inspection/compliance evidence to a public enforcement action represents an escalation in operational/regulatory information for facility-exposed issuers.
candidates.event_clock: public observation boundary of the enforcement state; inspection date and violation date are retained as event metadata but are not substituted for dissemination time.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: facility-to-issuer map shuffle preserving facility counts
force a one-session lag and compare only pre-specified semantic invariants

candidates.name: Patent citation provenance state
candidates.mechanism: The composition of examiner-originated versus applicant-originated citations on newly public patent documents is a fixed technology-information state distinct from raw patent counts or grant shocks.
candidates.event_clock: patent publication boundary; no later grant date or citation update may enter the historical prefix.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante

candidates.name: Government-demand shock propagation
candidates.mechanism: A newly public government-procurement award can change the observable demand state of directly exposed contractors; a fixed contractor/network exposure map supplies the economic transmission channel.
candidates.event_clock: historical public-observation boundary for the award state; action date or contract start date cannot be used as a substitute unless independently justified as publicly observable at the decision point.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: future-amendment mutation test preserving original award identifiers
gates: public-observation timestamp or conservative next-session boundary

candidates.name: Patent-publication shock
candidates.mechanism: Pre-grant publication of a patent application creates an ex-ante technology disclosure event; issuer exposure is fixed from the assignee/applicant identity before outcomes are read.
candidates.event_clock: official publication boundary of the patent application; later grant or prosecution updates are excluded from the historical prefix.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: randomize publication arrivals within the same calendar structure

candidates.name: Clinical-trial results first-posted shock
candidates.mechanism: The first public posting of structured clinical-trial results creates a distinct disclosure boundary; sponsor/issuer exposure is fixed independently of post-event market outcomes.
candidates.event_clock: Results First Posted time/date when available; Results First Posted with QC Comments is a later revision state and cannot overwrite the original public prefix.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no result-sign classification is required in the first PIT stage

candidates.name: Clinical-trial reporting deadline breach / missing-result state
candidates.mechanism: A publicly observable failure to provide required clinical-trial results by a fixed statutory reporting boundary is an information-absence event. The mechanism is distinct from the later content of the results themselves and may reflect selective or delayed disclosure.
candidates.event_clock: The first reproducible public snapshot on or after the fixed reporting deadline at which an applicable trial remains without publicly posted results, after excluding valid certification/extension states known by that boundary.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: shift the deadline boundary by one fixed session
inject future results or future corrections and require historical prefix invariance
treat a later FDAAA violation notice as if it were the original deadline-miss observation and require the inferred boundary to change
gates: historical version snapshots at the statutory boundary
literature_basis: Cochrane 2024, Time to publication for results of clinical trials (PMID 39601300)
Kim et al. 2017, The significance of the trial outcome was associated with publication rate and time to publication (PMID 28238789)

candidates.name: Government-demand award × ex-ante financing constraint
candidates.mechanism: A newly public federal procurement award can relax financing constraints and expand access to credit after award. Conditional on a fixed pre-event financing-constraint state, the same public-demand shock may therefore have a stronger or more persistent economic transmission than an unconditional award indicator.
candidates.event_clock: Historical public-observation boundary of the award state; award/action date cannot substitute for observation time unless independently proven.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: shuffle financing-constraint values within the frozen event universe
shift public-observation boundary by one fixed session
use post-award balance-sheet values and require the construction to fail closed
future-amendment mutation preserving original award identity
gates: frozen pre-event financing data from latest admissible public filing
literature_basis: Hebous & Zimmermann 2021, Can government demand stimulate private investment? Evidence from US federal procurement
Gabriel 2024, The credit channel of public procurement
2025, What Can 240,000 New Credit Transactions Tell Us About the Impact of NGEU Funds? (arXiv:2504.01964)

candidates.name: Public-information release-lag surprise
candidates.mechanism: The elapsed interval between an official source's earliest public-observation timestamp and a later, separately defined publication or process-stage date can itself measure information latency. The event remains about information arrival speed, not event content.
candidates.event_clock: The first reproducible public-observation timestamp supplied by the official source. Underlying occurrence/action/submission dates remain metadata and are not treated as public availability. A stage-to-stage gap is admissible only when both endpoints have independently documented semantics.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: randomize release timestamps within fixed calendar blocks
replace public-observation time with occurrence time and require a detectable contract change
use future latency distribution statistics and require fail-closed detection
same-day timestamp ambiguity must be excluded
gates: independently documented semantics for both endpoints of the latency interval
literature_basis: 2026 preprint, Fast Numbers, Slow Language: Bridging Quantitative and Qualitative Earnings Signals (arXiv:2606.29734)
2026 preprint, Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In? (arXiv:2608.14014)
2026 preprint, Time-Series Foundation Models That Understand Data Revisions (arXiv:2609.28576)

candidates.name: Labor-representation certification shock
candidates.mechanism: A newly public NLRB election outcome or certification changes the observable labor-representation state of an employer. The economic channel is potential labor-cost, bargaining-power and operational-governance change; no return sign is assumed ex ante.
candidates.event_clock: Earliest reproducible NLRB public result/certification boundary. Tally Issued Date is retained as source metadata; if no time-of-day can be proven, use the next regular trading-session boundary rather than infer an intraday clock.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign is assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: shift the public-result boundary by one to five trading sessions
permute employer-to-issuer mappings within the frozen event universe
randomize outcome labels while preserving election counts and calendar structure
inject later case updates/certifications and verify the historical prefix is unchanged
gates: public-observation clock or conservative next-session rule

candidates.name: Public-source observability gap
candidates.mechanism: Cross-channel information-diffusion state: an independent public/administrative event is already public before the issuer makes the same state explicit in formal disclosure. Use only the timing relationship at the issuer-disclosure boundary; do not duplicate upstream event content.
candidates.event_clock: Issuer first reproducible formal-disclosure boundary; external occurrence dates are metadata unless contemporaneous public availability is independently proven.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante

candidates.name: Macro-vintage revision exposure state
candidates.mechanism: Risk/reliability state for fixed firm/industry exposure to macro variables whose first-release values have historically characterized revision propensity, using prior real-time vintages only. It is not a macro-surprise return signal.
candidates.event_clock: First defensible public vintage/availability boundary; later vintages are diagnostic only.
candidates.direction: risk/reliability state; no return sign assumed ex ante

candidates.name: Cognitive processing friction decomposition
candidates.mechanism: Public corporate information can impose heterogeneous processing costs. Separate cognitive/processing friction from information quantity, document size and boilerplate rather than treating length as the mechanism. The first stage is a deterministic decomposition of SEC filing characteristics; no return ranking is allowed.
candidates.event_clock: Earliest admissible public SEC filing boundary for the frozen filing prefix; later amendments and normalized/current text cannot alter the historical prefix.
candidates.direction: two-sided processing/reliability state; no return sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: investor-sophistication or liquidity controls eliminate all separation
gates: accepted/public clock and immutable filing prefix
deterministic feature compiler with fixed formulas
fixed issuer/security mapping and amendment lineage
literature_basis: Du & Tang (2026), Cognitive Load and Information Processing in Financial Markets: Theory and Evidence from Disclosure Complexity, arXiv:2507.07037 v2
Cookson, Moon & Noh (2025), Speculative and Informative, Review of Corporate Finance Studies
candidates.risk_note: Must merge back into Q131 rather than remain separate if the decomposition is not empirically distinct.

candidates.name: Mandatory-voluntary disclosure semantic wedge
candidates.mechanism: Selective allocation of topics between mandatory and voluntary public disclosures can encode information beyond document size, complexity or generic sentiment.
candidates.event_clock: SEC acceptance timestamp for the filing/disclosure package; historical prefix frozen at the public boundary.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante

candidates.name: Filing-change x options-response information-processing wedge
candidates.mechanism: A public 10-K textual change followed by a post-filing option-volatility-smirk change represents a cross-market information-processing differential rather than an options-only signal.
candidates.event_clock: SEC acceptance timestamp; Q129 option observations are EOD and same-session use is prohibited unless tighter dissemination is proven.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante

candidates.name: Narrative-structured information representation gap
candidates.mechanism: Narrative filing change can be corroborated, absent or contradicted by contemporaneous structured XBRL fact changes; the state is representation mismatch, not generic novelty or length.
candidates.event_clock: SEC as-filed public filing boundary; later amendments/current text cannot rewrite the historical prefix.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: XBRL text-block/presentation mapping is incomplete or unstable across the frozen filing sample
gates: XBRL text-block and presentation-role structural mapping audit
candidates.critical_mapping_rule: Primary mapping must use reproducible XBRL text-block tags and presentation/relationship structure available in the as-filed filing. A free-form post-outcome semantic topic-to-concept mapping is prohibited. If a section cannot be mapped mechanically, the observation is excluded rather than manually reassigned.
source_basis: XBRL International Inline XBRL Block Tagging 1.0 Working Group Note (2024)

candidates.name: Government R&D to procurement-option-value state
candidates.mechanism: Some federal R&D awards can embed an option-like path to future procurement; competition structure and pre-event capability are part of the information mechanism rather than award size alone.
candidates.event_clock: Earliest defensible historical public-observation boundary for the award; action/modification dates are metadata unless public observability is proven.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: future production contracts leak into features
historical archive publication lag cannot be deterministically mapped to award transaction visibility
gates: documented USAspending publication-frequency rule and historical archive availability audit
candidates.implementation_note: The first PIT subgate may use the documented USAspending prime-award publication schedule as a conservative public-observation boundary only after confirming the schedule applies to the exact transaction class and historical period. Action date remains metadata.

candidates.name: Technology disclosure–verification credibility gap
candidates.mechanism: A firm's public narrative about adoption or implementation of an emerging technology can diverge from independently observable implementation evidence. The mechanism is the credibility gap between disclosed claims and externally verifiable action, not narrative length, generic novelty, or the narrative-vs-structured-XBRL representation mismatch in Q220.
candidates.event_clock: SEC as-filed acceptance timestamp; historical filing prefix frozen at that public boundary. External implementation evidence must use its own reproducible historical public-observation boundary and may not be looked up after the event to label the original state.
features: fixed technology-claim intensity in as-filed SEC narrative
independently verifiable historical implementation indicator from predeclared public evidence
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: Q220 structured-representation gap fully explains the decomposition
implementation evidence publication lag cannot be bounded historically
post-event implementation evidence leaks into the event state
technology taxonomy is not reproducible from predeclared rules
gates: historical SEC filing archive with accepted/as-filed boundary
historical public implementation evidence with reproducible observation clock
frozen technology taxonomy and deterministic claim extractor
separate disclosure and implementation lineage audit
literature_basis: Jiang, Song & An (2026), Corporate fuzzy disclosure, investors’ limited attention, and capital market overreaction, Journal of Innovation & Knowledge, available online 2026-09-01
AI washing: Strategic disclosure and backlash (2026), Finance Research Letters 95, 109684
Digital narrative inflation and corporate innovation: Evidence from large language model semantic scoring (2026), Finance Research Letters, forthcoming issue
candidates.risk_note: Merge back into Q220 if external verification adds no empirically distinct mechanism or cannot be given a defensible historical public-observation clock.

candidates.name: EDGAR document-demand intensity / acquisition shock
candidates.mechanism: A public regulatory filing can generate observable post-release acquisition demand in the SEC EDGAR access logs. The mechanism is revealed document-acquisition demand after disclosure, distinct from filing content, complexity, generic external attention, ownership change, or dissemination breadth.
candidates.event_clock: SEC filing acceptance/public boundary; requests are evaluated only at timestamps strictly after the frozen public boundary.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
source_basis: SEC EDGAR Log File Data Sets
SEC Variables for EDGAR Log File Data Sets
Li & Sun 2022 Information acquisition and expected returns
Lee & Lee 2026 Observable Versus Unobservable Information Acquisition
candidates.implementation_note: Initial feasibility is restricted to the modern SEC log schema (2020-05-19 through 2025-06-30). The 2017-2020 gap and legacy schema differences must remain explicit; no historical splice is permitted without a separate bridge.
candidates.measurement_warning: Observed EDGAR acquisition is an observable trace, not latent information demand. Public observability can itself change research behaviour; low observed demand must therefore not be interpreted monotonically.

candidates.name: SEC FOIA information-acquisition state
candidates.mechanism: A costly, targeted FOIA request to the SEC reveals a requester's information-acquisition intent about a firm or economically relevant matter. The mechanism differs from EDGAR document access because the requester seeks records held by the regulator that are not simply public archive traffic.
candidates.event_clock: Two-clock contract: latent acquisition clock = FOIA request submission date; public-observation clock = earliest SEC FOIA-log publication boundary that makes the request visible to the market. Any public-data trading feature must be frozen at the latter boundary or later; request submission is retained only as a historical latent-event attribute.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: request_target_cannot_be mapped_to_frozen issuer identities without hindsight
literature_basis: Bao, Brendel, Drake & Su (2026), The information content of private information acquisition: evidence from FOIA requests to the SEC, Review of Accounting Studies
candidates.implementation_note: Start with the currently published SEC monthly FOIA CSVs and a conservative post-2013 window unless 2006-2012 public availability is independently reconstructed. The research literature shows that SEC publication frequency changed from retrospective/annual-or-quarterly to monthly and that short-window incorporation is weak while monthly-publication periods strengthen observable effects. Therefore a tradable Q227 contract must use the log-publication boundary, not the private request date, as the public signal clock. Entity mapping is a first-order gate because SEC FOIA logs expose requester/request-description fields rather than a canonical issuer CIK. Do not use closure/disposition to define the public signal.
candidates.measurement_warning: FOIA request activity can reveal costly private information before the market sees it, while the public monthly log creates a delayed observation channel. Public-data strategies must not backdate the signal to request submission. Low observed public request activity can also reflect requester substitution or reduced observable behaviour after publication becomes more frequent.

candidates.name: SEC filing-review dialogue / disclosure-scrutiny state
candidates.mechanism: Public SEC comment-letter and filer-response dialogue can reveal regulatory scrutiny, unresolved disclosure questions and review friction that are not reducible to raw filing complexity, mandatory/voluntary disclosure allocation, enforcement or generic release latency.
candidates.event_clock: Earliest public release boundary of SEC filing-review correspondence; latent review start is metadata only. If exact time is unproven, use the next regular trading-session boundary.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
literature_basis: Bozanic, Dietrich & Johnson (2017), SEC comment letters and firm disclosure
Johnston (2017), Regulatory Oversight of Financial Reporting: Securities and Exchange Commission Comment Letters
candidates.implementation_note: SEC says filing-review correspondence has been publicly released since 2005 and current guidance places publication at least 20 business days after effectiveness/review completion. The public correspondence clock must therefore be treated separately from the latent SEC review clock.

candidates.name: Regulator-disclosed consumer complaint / management-response information state
candidates.mechanism: Public regulator complaint records can reveal operational problems through complaint topic/severity and the subsequent company-response process. The economically relevant object is complaint-to-response state, not raw complaint volume or generic sentiment.
candidates.event_clock: Two-clock contract: latent complaint receipt/submission date; tradable public-observation boundary = earliest defensible publication boundary. Response information enters only when public.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
source_basis: Cai et al. 2026 consumer complaints and managerial responses

candidates.name: Cross-capital-structure bond-implied equity information state
candidates.mechanism: Corporate bond investors and equity investors can incorporate shared firm information at different speeds. An issuer-level bond-implied state or bond/equity disagreement may therefore expose information not yet reflected in equity prices.
candidates.event_clock: Public FINRA TRACE end-of-day observation boundary; only freely accessible data may be used. Bond observations must precede the equity decision boundary under a conservative session rule.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
source_basis: Auh & Kim 2026 Across the Capital Structure: Bond Signals and Equity Returns
Keshavarz & Sirmans 2026 Momentum Across the Capital Structure
candidates.implementation_note: Issuer-level bond state must be orthogonalized against broad rates and the freely accessible FINRA Corporate Debt Market Breadth/Sentiment state before any later outcome test. This control is predeclared and is not itself an alpha candidate. The public trade-structure fields documented by FINRA (Trade Status, As-Of, Side, Contra Party Type, Reporting Party Type, etc.) are to be treated first as provenance/robustness controls, not alpha. Their admissibility is conditional on the exact free EOD route exposing the field consistently across the frozen historical panel. Future corrections/cancellations may be used only as a mutation/exclusion-sensitivity audit; they must never rewrite the historical decision prefix. FINRA documents a free proprietary fixed-income Symbol and public issuer-name/security attributes; Q230 should prefer these free identifiers when the frozen EOD historical route exposes them consistently, and must not introduce a paid CUSIP dependency merely to solve identity. Current-vs-historical issuer mapping remains a separate PIT gate.

blocked_or_composite_tracks.Q193: Composition remains prohibited until contributing component channels independently pass candidate-specific PIT.
blocked_or_composite_tracks.Q198: Historical Federal Register Public Inspection By-Date API route is now source-feasible and a four-date PIT clock census completed. Candidate-specific correction/withdrawal lineage, entity mapping and independent reproduction remain required.
